channel.title: PsyDigest — psychiatry literature digest
channel.description: Summaries of new psychiatric research and guidelines

item.title: Dose-dependent efficacy and safety of centanafadine in patients with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: A systematic review of the latest evidence.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review assessed the efficacy and safety of centanafadine, a multimodal norepinephrine-dopamine-serotonin reuptake inhibitor (NDSRI), for ADHD across pediatric, adolescent, and adult populations using randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials. The review synthesized dose-response patterns and adverse events narratively due to heterogeneity in study designs.
FINDINGS: Four RCTs (1,845 participants) were included. In children, high-dose centanafadine significantly improved ADHD-RS-5 scores vs. placebo (-16.3 vs. -10.8; p < 0.001), while low-dose did not (MD -2.7; 95% CI -6.0 to 0.5; p = 0.10). In adolescents, 328.8 mg improved ADHD-RS-5 scores (MD -4.3; p = 0.0006; Cohen’s d = -0.40), but 164.4 mg did not (p = 0.3016). In adults, both 200 mg and 400 mg/day significantly improved AISRS scores (LSMDs -2.74 to -4.42; p ≤ 0.039). Treatment-emergent adverse events ranged from 25%–39% in children, 23.8%–50.3% in adolescents, and 17.6%–31.8% in adults, with higher rates at higher doses in some groups.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence suggests dose-dependent efficacy of centanafadine, particularly in children and adolescents, with smaller but significant effects in adults. However, the review highlights critical limitations: only four RCTs from three publications, short-term follow-up, no active comparators, and potential industry sponsorship bias. The effect sizes (e.g., Cohen’s d = -0.40 in adolescents) are modest and may not translate to clinically meaningful improvements for all patients. The safety profile appears dose-related, warranting caution in dosing.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Centanafadine may offer an additional treatment option for ADHD, but its place in therapy remains uncertain due to limited long-term data and lack of comparative trials. Clinicians should weigh modest efficacy against adverse effects and await further independent, head-to-head studies before considering it a first-line agent.

item.title: Exercise-based interventions for postpartum depressive symptoms: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of exercise modality and weekly volume.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and network meta-analysis examined randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of exercise-based interventions for postpartum depressive symptoms, comparing exercise modalities and weekly volumes using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). The study synthesized evidence to determine whether exercise reduces depressive symptoms and if specific types or doses are more effective.
FINDINGS: Twenty-four RCTs with 1,792 participants (912 intervention, 880 control) were included. Exercise significantly reduced EPDS scores compared to usual care/non-exercise controls (MD = -2.73, 95% CI -3.57 to -1.88; I² = 95%). Yoga/mind-body exercise ranked highest in the exercise-type network (SUCRA = 94.2%), with a modest estimated advantage over aerobic exercise (MD = -2.62, 95% CI -5.16 to -0.08). The 45–90 min/week volume category ranked highest (SUCRA = 84.6%), but no between-volume contrasts were statistically significant. Subgroup analysis suggested shorter interventions (<12 weeks) had larger effects than longer ones (≥12 weeks), but this was exploratory.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence suggests exercise may modestly reduce postpartum depressive symptoms, but high heterogeneity, indirect comparisons, and very low network certainty limit confidence in identifying an optimal exercise type or dose. The star-shaped network and mixed samples (prevention vs. treatment) further constrain conclusions. While exercise may serve as a useful adjunct, it should not replace clinical assessment or indicated treatments like psychotherapy or pharmacotherapy.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Exercise can be considered a low-risk adjunct in postpartum mental health care, particularly for mild symptoms, but clinicians should individualize recommendations and monitor response. The lack of clear dose-response or modality superiority means treatment choices should prioritize patient preference and feasibility over theoretical advantages.

item.title: Ketamine and Esketamine in Acute Suicidal Presentations: Evidence, Limits, and a Conceptual Recovery-Enabling Downstaging Framework.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on intravenous racemic ketamine and intranasal esketamine for acute suicidal presentations in adults, aiming to clarify which outcomes these interventions affect and how they fit into emergency suicide care pathways. It prioritizes randomized trials, meta-analyses, and regulatory documents but does not perform formal risk-of-bias assessment or pooled analysis.
FINDINGS: Intravenous ketamine shows randomized and meta-analytic evidence for short-term reduction in suicidal ideation in selected adults, though effects vary by population, comparator, and follow-up duration. Intranasal esketamine (ASPIRE trials) accelerated improvement in depressive symptoms in hospitalized patients with major depressive disorder and acute suicidal ideation, but did not consistently outperform placebo in reducing suicidality. Neither intervention has evidence for preventing suicide attempts or deaths.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is limited by the lack of formal risk-of-bias assessment and absence of pooled reanalysis, reducing confidence in effect estimates. The short-term nature of observed benefits and lack of impact on hard outcomes (attempts/deaths) constrain clinical utility. The proposed "downstaging framework" is conceptual and unvalidated, offering a theoretical approach rather than evidence-based guidance.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Ketamine/esketamine may offer short-term symptomatic relief in carefully selected patients but should not be viewed as suicide-preventive. They must be integrated into comprehensive emergency care, including safety planning and risk formulation, without replacing standard interventions.

item.title: Effects of VR interventions on pediatric ADHD: a systematic review, meta-analysis and exploratory machine-learning analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined the efficacy of virtual reality (VR) interventions on clinically distinct outcome domains in children and adolescents with ADHD, synthesizing randomized and quasi-experimental controlled studies to assess effects across ADHD/behavioral symptoms, executive/cognitive function, social/emotional function, and motor/visual-perceptual function.
FINDINGS: Across 13 studies (n=928), pooled Hedges' g values were 0.49 (95% CI -0.59 to 1.57) for ADHD/behavioral symptoms, 1.15 (95% CI 0.38 to 1.92) for executive/cognitive function, 0.51 (95% CI 0.08 to 0.93) for social/emotional function, and 0.88 (95% CI 0.02 to 1.74) for motor/visual-perceptual function. The all-domain composite effect was g=0.98 (95% CI 0.47 to 1.50), with substantial heterogeneity (I²=91.7%) and a prediction interval crossing the null (-0.69 to 2.65). No serious adverse events were reported, but safety data were inconsistently recorded.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is small, heterogeneous, and at high risk of bias, yielding very low GRADE certainty across all domains. While executive/cognitive function shows the most consistent signal (g=1.15), the wide confidence intervals and prediction interval crossing zero suggest that effects may not be robust or generalizable. The lack of reliable explanations for heterogeneity and inconsistent safety reporting further limit confidence. The findings are preliminary and do not support superiority of VR across domains or consistent clinical effects.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: VR may hold promise as an adjunctive intervention for ADHD-related cognitive and functional outcomes, particularly executive function, but current evidence is insufficient to recommend routine use. Clinicians should await larger, well-controlled trials with standardized outcome measures and safety reporting before considering VR as a standard adjunctive therapy.

item.title: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline: Management of Menopause-Related Vasomotor, Sleep, and Mood Symptoms.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline addresses the management of vasomotor symptoms (e.g., hot flashes), sleep disturbances, and mood symptoms in perimenopausal and postmenopausal individuals (assigned female at birth, including women, transgender men, and gender-diverse individuals) aged 40 or older. It synthesizes evidence to provide recommendations for pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic interventions.
FINDINGS: The guideline was developed using a structured protocol with a multidisciplinary writing team and applied a modified GRADE framework to assess evidence quality. Recommendations are graded by strength and evidence quality, with ungraded Good Practice Points included where evidence was insufficient. Specific effect sizes, confidence intervals, or p-values are not reported in the abstract.
INTERPRETATION: The strength of this guideline lies in its structured, evidence-based approach using GRADE methodology, which enhances transparency and reliability of recommendations. However, the abstract does not provide detailed quantitative outcomes or comparative data, limiting assessment of clinical significance. The inclusion of diverse populations (e.g., transgender men, gender-diverse individuals) improves external validity, but applicability to routine psychiatric care may be limited since the focus is on gynecologic and general medical management rather than psychiatric interventions.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This guideline may inform clinicians about evidence-based options for managing menopause-related symptoms but does not directly address psychiatric treatments such as antidepressants or psychotherapy for mood symptoms. Clinicians should consider the guideline’s recommendations in the context of psychiatric care, particularly when mood symptoms are prominent, but should remain cautious due to the lack of detailed quantitative data in the abstract.

item.title: Artificial intelligence EEG biomarkers for schizophrenia diagnosis: Systematic review with PROBAST+AI assessment.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The review asks whether artificial-intelligence-enhanced resting-state EEG can reliably diagnose schizophrenia, synthesizing 43 studies (N = 6 584) under PRISMA guidance and rating risk of bias with PROBAST+AI.
FINDINGS: Pooled diagnostic accuracy was 93.38 % (deep learning 96.83 % vs classical ML 87.68 %). Only 4.7 % of studies used external validation; subject-wise validation yielded 88.22 % accuracy versus 98.14 % with segment-wise protocols, indicating data leakage. High risk of bias was present in 76.7 % of studies, mainly due to flawed data partitioning and lack of independent verification.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is methodologically weak: accuracies are likely inflated by data leakage and inadequate validation. The PROBAST+AI assessment shows high risk of bias in most studies, so the reported effect sizes cannot be trusted for clinical decision-making. Standardized, transparent validation is urgently needed before any bedside application.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current AI-EEG biomarkers for schizophrenia diagnosis should not be adopted in routine care; centers should await externally validated, low-bias models before considering implementation.

item.title: Psychoeducational interventions for children and adolescents with potentially traumatic experiences: a systematic review.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review (PROSPERO-registered) examined whether stand-alone psychoeducational interventions improve knowledge, psychopathology, or functioning in children/adolescents with potentially traumatic experiences (PTEs). The clinical question is whether such low-threshold interventions can mitigate distress after trauma.
FINDINGS: Seven heterogeneous studies (k=7) were included. Two of three studies on trauma-related knowledge showed improvements (e.g., PTSD knowledge, posttraumatic growth), while one found no effect. Among five symptom-focused studies, two reported reduced anxiety and one reduced PTSD symptoms in highly distressed subgroups; other outcomes (sleep, depression, anger, dissociation) were non-significant. One study reported improved psychosocial functioning. No studies addressed interpersonal or complex trauma.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is very small (seven studies), methodologically diverse, and often underpowered, limiting firm conclusions. Positive findings are confined to specific outcomes and subgroups, with null results across most measures. High risk of bias and lack of long-term follow-up further weaken confidence. The review highlights major gaps (e.g., complex trauma) and calls for rigorous RCTs with standardized outcomes and longer follow-up.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current evidence does not support psychoeducation as a stand-alone trauma-specific treatment, but it may serve as a low-risk, accessible preventive or early psychoeducational step. Clinicians should avoid relying on it for symptom reduction in the absence of stronger data, and prioritize evidence-based trauma therapies when indicated.

item.title: Clinical outcomes following five-day accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation for treatment-resistant depression in routine clinical practice: A prospective naturalistic cohort study.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This single-centre, open-label, uncontrolled prospective naturalistic cohort study examined whether a 5-day accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (aiTBS) protocol (30 sessions, 18 000 pulses) is feasible, tolerable and clinically effective for adults with treatment-resistant depression (TRD) in major depressive disorder (MDD) or bipolar II disorder (BP-II).
FINDINGS: Forty-six adults (mean age 44.3 y, 54.4 % male) received 5-day aiTBS. HAMD-17 response rates were 28.3 % immediately post-treatment and 37.0 % at 2-month follow-up; remission rates were 26.1 % and 32.6 %, respectively. PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores also improved. CGI-I showed 52.2 % improved post-treatment and 60.9 % at follow-up. Adverse events were mainly transient stimulation-site pain.
INTERPRETATION: The study demonstrates feasibility and tolerability of 5-day aiTBS in routine practice, with moderate short-term symptom reductions. However, the single-arm, unblinded design and lack of sham control preclude ruling out placebo effects or expectancy bias. The sample is modest, limiting precision of effect estimates. Randomised sham-controlled trials are required to confirm efficacy and durability.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: At present, 5-day aiTBS may be considered an experimental option for TRD when standard iTBS is impractical, but patients should be counselled that evidence for efficacy is preliminary and equipoise remains.

item.title: App-Based Stabilization Phase Within Blended Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy With Compassion for Adolescents With Posttraumatic Stress Disorder: Formative Qualitative Study.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This formative qualitative pretrial study examined the acceptability and feasibility of an app-based stabilization phase integrated into blended trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy with compassion (bTF-CBT-C) for adolescent girls (aged 14–16 years) with PTSD. The goal was to inform the design of a future pilot RCT by exploring user experiences, caregiver support needs, and clinical workflow integration.
FINDINGS: Four adolescent girls completed a 5-week app-based stabilization program combining TF-CBT coping skills and compassion-focused practices, with five caregivers receiving parallel content in a non-app format. Qualitative interviews with three adolescents and four caregivers, plus a survey of four clinicians, revealed fluctuating engagement influenced by emotional capacity, cognitive load, family strain, and technical issues. Participants found the content meaningful and grounding but noted challenges with fatigue, school demands, neurodivergent attention patterns, and unclear caregiver roles. Clinicians emphasized the need for scaffolding, reminders, and reliable access.
INTERPRETATION: This small, qualitative study (n=4 adolescents, n=5 caregivers, n=4 clinicians) suggests potential acceptability and feasibility of app-based stabilization within bTF-CBT-C, but findings are preliminary and context-dependent. The thematic analysis highlights important design considerations—flexible pacing, cognitive accessibility, caregiver guidance, and technical reliability—rather than definitive clinical outcomes. The lack of quantitative outcomes, small sample, and focus on a specific subgroup (adolescent girls) limit generalizability. The study is valuable for refining the intervention before a pilot RCT but does not establish efficacy or effectiveness.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These findings support continued development of app-based stabilization phases in trauma therapy for adolescents, with attention to user-centered design and caregiver involvement. However, routine adoption is not yet justified; results should guide iterative improvements and be tested in controlled trials before informing clinical practice.

item.title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Preliminary Outcomes of a Group-Based Brief Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy Protocol for Suicide Prevention in a Brazilian Public Mental Health Service: A Mixed-Methods Pilot Study.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This single-arm, nonrandomized mixed-methods pilot study in a Brazilian public psychiatric outpatient service evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary outcomes of a group-adapted brief cognitive-behavioral therapy protocol (BCBT) for suicide prevention in 27 adults across two cohorts.
FINDINGS: Enrollment targets were met, with 70.4% attending ≥4 sessions and no intervention-related adverse events reported. All six questionnaire respondents rated the intervention 8–10 for recommendation, and qualitative feedback highlighted shared suffering recognition and instillation of hope. Weekly suicidal ideation (BSI) showed a nonsignificant linear slope (B = −0.29, p = 0.129), but multiple imputation yielded B = −0.36 (p = 0.018). An exploratory quadratic model suggested greater decline later in treatment (p = 0.008). Among 18 participants with ≥4 sessions and baseline BSI, scores decreased by 8.2 points (d = −0.67; p = 0.011).
INTERPRETATION: The study demonstrates preliminary feasibility and acceptability of group-adapted BCBT in a resource-limited public setting, with no safety concerns. However, the uncontrolled design precludes causal inference; the small sample and reliance on multiple imputation for significance weaken internal validity. The observed effect size (d = −0.67) is moderate but derived from a subset, and the clinical significance of an 8.2-point BSI reduction is uncertain without a comparator or longer follow-up. Further randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm efficacy and durability.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This pilot suggests group BCBT may be feasible in public psychiatric services, but routine adoption is premature. Clinicians should await controlled trials before considering implementation, while monitoring for potential benefits in patient-reported hope and shared experience.

item.title: Keeping the body in mind: Development of the Transdiagnostic Global Impression-Somatic Symptoms and Signs (TGI-3S) scale.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Routine assessment of physical health in psychiatric patients is clinically important but lacks brief, validated tools. This study reports the development of the Transdiagnostic Global Impression-Somatic Symptoms and Signs (TGI-3S) scale, a brief front-end screening instrument for somatic burden in patients with any mental disorder.
FINDINGS: The TGI-3S was created through deductive item generation, two expert panel validations, and two iterative usability-testing rounds with patients and caregivers. In the final usability round (n not specified), 96% found the aim clear, 87% rated instructions as easy to follow, 72% completed the scale in under 5 minutes, and burden was rated low with good item comprehension.
INTERPRETATION: The study describes an early-stage scale development process with promising usability metrics, but no psychometric validation data are yet available. The small usability sample and lack of reported reliability, validity, or inter-rater metrics limit confidence in the instrument’s performance. The TGI-3S may eventually support routine somatic screening, but clinical adoption should await full validation.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: For now, the TGI-3S remains a candidate tool rather than a recommended instrument; clinicians should continue using established measures for somatic assessment in psychiatric care until psychometric data are published.

item.title: Longitudinal peripheral DNA methylation remodeling following ketamine-assisted psychotherapy in major depressive disorder.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This longitudinal cohort study in 10 adults with major depressive disorder (MDD) examined whether peripheral DNA methylation changes accompany clinical improvement after three sessions of intranasal ketamine combined with structured psychotherapy, addressing the molecular underpinnings of ketamine’s sustained antidepressant effects.
FINDINGS: Mean Beck Depression Inventory-II scores fell from the severe to the mild range after treatment (p < .001). Of 802,595 CpG sites, 20,770 met a nominal post- vs pre-treatment methylation change threshold; after filtering for magnitude and stability, 962 CpGs remained, including 517 annotated genes. A linear mixed-effects model across 603 preselected loci highlighted NOTCH1-related Reactome pathways driven by NOTCH1, DLL1, and ADAM17, suggesting coordinated Notch signaling changes.
INTERPRETATION: The study provides preliminary evidence of a structured peripheral methylation signature linked to clinical improvement, but the sample is tiny, lacks a comparator arm, and methylation was measured in buccal cells rather than brain tissue. The exploratory enrichment analysis was not independently validated, so causality and brain relevance remain uncertain. The effect size of symptom change is large, yet the methylation findings are hypothesis-generating only.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These results do not yet alter practice; they suggest potential epigenetic biomarkers for further study, but routine use of methylation testing to guide ketamine-assisted psychotherapy is not supported by this evidence.

item.title: Stimulant Persistence in Adult ADHD: A Retrospective Analysis of a Large Clinical Cohort.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study compared 12-month persistence of dexamphetamine (dAMP) versus methylphenidate (MPH) in adults with ADHD in a large multicentre cohort, addressing a gap in long-term comparative evidence suggested by short-term network meta-analyses.
FINDINGS: Among 12,995 adults (49% female), 62% initiated dAMP and 38% MPH. Median time-to-transition (switching class, non-stimulant transition, or discontinuation) was 33.1 weeks for dAMP vs 15.0 weeks for MPH. MPH had a 45% higher hazard of non-persistence than dAMP (HR = 1.45, 95% CI [1.36–1.55]). Hyperactive/impulsive presentation (HR = 1.14, p = 0.025) and objective impulsivity (HR = 1.05, p = 0.002) were associated with non-persistence; dAMP’s persistence advantage increased with higher motor activity (interaction p = 0.003).
INTERPRETATION: The large sample and robust Cox model with clinician-level random effects strengthen internal validity, though the retrospective design and lack of randomisation limit causal inference. The effect size (HR ≈ 1.45) is statistically strong and clinically plausible, suggesting a meaningful persistence advantage for dAMP. However, unmeasured confounding (e.g., prescribing bias, patient preference) and absence of blinding or placebo control temper certainty. External validity is supported by multicentre data but may not fully reflect routine care outside specialist settings.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These findings support considering dAMP over MPH when prioritising long-term adherence in adults with ADHD, particularly in those with higher hyperactive/impulsive symptoms. Clinicians should monitor persistence and tolerability, recognising that persistence is not equivalent to efficacy or safety.

item.title: Undirected and directed networks of problem gambling: Follow the money trail.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This psychometric network analysis examined which symptoms of problem gambling (PG) are most central in undirected and directed models, using four Norwegian population surveys (2013, 2015, 2019, 2022; age 16–74). The goal was to identify core symptoms that could guide screening and early intervention.
FINDINGS: In undirected networks (n ≈ 3 200–6 000 per wave), financial problems showed the highest strength centrality. Network generalizability was strong between 2019 and 2022 (p = .65; φ = .79; r = .85). In directed cross-lagged models (n = 3 043 and n = 2 749), borrowing money had the strongest out-strength (predicting later symptoms), while guilt had the highest in-strength (being most predicted by earlier symptoms). Generalizability between the two follow-up periods was inconclusive (φ = .08; r = .74).
INTERPRETATION: The evidence is preliminary but consistent in highlighting financial processes as central to PG networks. Strengths include large, representative samples and rigorous network validation. However, directed-network generalizability was weak, and causal inference is limited by observational design and self-report expenditure data. The clinical significance of targeting “financial problems” or “borrowing money” remains untested in intervention studies.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These findings suggest financial indicators may be useful screening targets, but routine practice should not change until prospective studies demonstrate that intervening on these nodes reduces gambling severity.

item.title: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: transition to psychotic disorders.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This perspective article examines why some individuals with ADHD transition to psychotic disorders, a clinically important but under-recognized risk. It synthesizes hypotheses on mechanisms and treatment effects to guide risk stratification and secondary care prioritization.
FINDINGS: ADHD is associated with 4.7–8.9-fold increased odds of later psychotic disorders. Methylphenidate treatment does not appear to increase this risk, while data for amphetamines remain uncertain. Direct evidence linking early ADHD features to prodromal psychotic symptoms is limited, and mediation by environmental exposures is unproven.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is largely observational and inferential, with no primary data presented in this perspective. The large odds ratios are derived from prior studies and may be confounded by shared risk factors. The lack of direct support for prodromal models and mediation analyses limits mechanistic conclusions. The discussion of treatment safety is based on indirect evidence and highlights uncertainty for amphetamines.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Clinicians should remain vigilant for emerging psychotic symptoms in patients with ADHD, especially those with severe or treatment-resistant ADHD, but routine antipsychotic prophylaxis is not warranted. Primary care can manage less complex ADHD, reserving specialist follow-up for high-risk cases pending better stratification tools.

item.title: Turkish Validation of Assessment of Bullying Experiences Questionnaire for Neurodivergent Youth.
item.description: PURPOSE: Bullying is an important public health concern, particularly for neurodivergent youth who are at heightened risk for peer victimization. The aim of this study was to adapt the Assessment of Bullying Experiences (ABE) Questionnaire into Turkish and to evaluate its psychometric properties among neurodivergent youth. METHODS: The sample included 47 typically developing controls, 89 adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), 57 autistic individuals, and 58 with co-occurring autism and ADHD. Participants were recruited from three cities in Türkiye.

item.title: Global trends in adolescent school loneliness from 2000 to 2022: An analysis of gender and socioeconomic inequalities across 87 countries.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Despite concerns over increasing adolescent loneliness and its lasting negative impact on mental and physical health, global trends and the gender and socioeconomic inequalities remain unclear. The study examined trends in adolescent school loneliness from 2000 to 2022 across 87 countries, analyzing disparities by gender, socioeconomic status, and country-income level. METHODS: We analyzed data from the Programme for International Student Assessment, a nationally representative survey of 15-year-olds conducted in 2000, 2003, 2012, 2015, 2018, and 2022.

item.title: The severity of treatment-resistant depression and the response to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation: a prospective, observational, multi-center clinical cohort study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The Maudsley Staging Method (MSM) is a multidimensional framework for grading treatment resistance in depression (TRD); however, its ability to predict clinical response to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between MSM-graded treatment resistance and clinical response during rTMS.To investigate links between MSM scores, longitudinal changes in patient-reported depressive symptoms, and mental well-being.

item.title: Obsessional jealousy: Provisional research criteria and report of 34 cases.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Obsessional jealousy is described in DSM-5 under Other Specified Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorders, yet operationalized criteria and clinical characterization are lacking. This study aimed to develop and field-test provisional research criteria for obsessional jealousy and describe the clinical features of individuals meeting these criteria. METHODS: Provisional research criteria were developed based on DSM-5 descriptions and applied in a self-referred sample of individuals reporting problematic jealousy (n = 58).

item.title: Longitudinal DNA methylation dynamics distinguish persistent and remitted attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in childhood and adolescence.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder, with symptoms that remit or persist over time. Biological mechanisms underlying symptom change remain poorly understood, though epigenetic processes, like DNA methylation (DNAm), may serve as dynamic biomarkers of clinical outcomes. We examined change in DNAm in children and adolescents with and without ADHD, including differences between remitted and persistent ADHD.

item.title: Shared genetic architecture between premenstrual disorder symptoms and major psychiatric disorders suggests a role for calcium signaling.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Major psychiatric disorders (MPDs) and premenstrual disorders (PMDs) are often comorbid, with indications of shared genetic architecture. However, the specific genetic variants underlying this comorbidity remain elusive. The aim of this study was to identify genomic loci shared between MPDs and PMDs, and to assess the functional characteristics of genes mapped to these loci.

item.title: Mental health of nurses and doctors in Ukraine during wartime: nationwide cross-sectional survey.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Since the full-scale Russian invasion in 2022, health facilities and healthcare workers in Ukraine have been systematically targeted. Despite growing calls to prioritise their mental health, robust evidence on the magnitude of the problem and its determinants remains limited. AIMS: To estimate the prevalence of mental health problems among doctors and nurses in Ukraine, and examine their association with key exposures. METHOD: We conducted a cross-sectional survey between May and September of 2025, in a non-probabilistic sample of doctors and nurses working in Ukraine.

item.title: From prediction to mechanism: rethinking PTSD treatment non-response through an iron-inflammation framework.
item.description: Precision psychiatry has improved prediction of treatment response across psychiatry, but translating biomarkers into treatment strategy remains difficult. Using PTSD as a model, we outline an iron-inflammation framework linking treatment-predictive neural circuitry to an upstream biological mechanism, illustrating how neuroimaging may support biologically informed stratification and targeted adjunctive treatments.

item.title: Lung cancer incidence, metastatic disease and mortality in people accessing mental health services: Opportunities for screening.
item.description: OBJECTIVE: To describe lung cancer incidence, stage and post-diagnosis mortality in people accessing mental health services, focusing on people aged 50-70 targeted by Australia's new lung cancer screening programme. METHODS: Linkage to the New South Wales Cancer Registry identified 39,680 lung cancer notifications from 2011 to 2020. Mental health services contact was defined as public mental health hospital or community care in the 5 years before cancer diagnosis.

item.title: Sudden Death in Schizophrenia.
item.description: Sudden death in schizophrenia is a commonly encountered history in forensic pathology. Most of these deaths, upon investigation and autopsy, are natural, usually relating to cardiovascular disease. In some instances, schizophrenia itself has been proposed as a cause of death. However, often schizophrenic patients are also on long-term medications with multiple dangerous side effects, many of which are not well represented in the forensic literature.

item.title: Access to antipsychotic in Brazil: using risk management to assess changes in pharmaceutical services.
item.description: The treatment of schizophrenia is essential for patients' quality of life and relies on the continuous use of antipsychotics provided by the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS). This study aimed to compare the processes that affect access to antipsychotics across different components of pharmaceutical services (PS) using risk management. The risk management methodology applied establishes risk levels, from very low to very high, based on the combination of probability and impact scales, following consecutive stages from context understanding to risk treatment.

item.title: Epigenetics processes involved in schizophrenia and antipsychotic treatment.
item.description: Schizophrenia is a severe psychiatric disorder characterized by abnormalities of thought, behavior, cognition, and affect. Risk factors for schizophrenia include a family history of psychosis, obstetric complications, childhood trauma, urban living, illicit substance use, and social isolation. It has long been concluded that there is a genetic component contributing to the development of schizophrenia; however, research studies in the pregenomic, postgenomic, and multiomics eras failed to illustrate the mechanisms underlying the genetic basis for this complex disease.

item.title: AANA Journal Course-Trauma-Informed Care Considerations for Anesthesia Providers.
item.description: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a prevalent, underrecognized condition among adults undergoing surgical procedures requiring anesthesia that poses significant risks throughout the perioperative period. Elements inherent to anesthesia care (e.g., loss of control, anesthetic induction, and emergence) may trigger trauma re-experiencing, resulting in heightened anxiety, dissociation, altered pain perception, and an increased incidence of emergence delirium.

item.title: Substance use diagnoses among patients who present to federally run mental health facilities with co-morbid ADHD and bipolar disorder between 2013-2023: a national analysis using random forest methods.
item.description: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Although substance use disorder is common in patients with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder or bipolar disorder, limited recent data exist for those with these co-occurring conditions. Our study analyzes recent trends and predictors of these diagnoses. METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of 2013-2023 Mental Health Client-Level Data, identifying patients with co-morbid ADHD and bipolar disorder and their SUD prevalence. Joinpoint regression was used to analyze trends, and random forest models identified the most important predictors.

item.title: Ophthalmologic manifestations in children with autism spectrum disorder.
item.description: PURPOSE: To determine the frequency and clinical characteristics of ophthalmologic manifestations in children aged ≤16 years with autism spectrum disorder who were evaluated at a private academic healthcare network and a public tertiary hospital. METHODS: This retrospective descriptive study was conducted through a review of the medical records of children aged <16 years with autism spectrum disorder who were examined between 2023 and 2024. Demographic characteristics, visual function testability, refractive errors, strabismus, and prescribed treatments were analyzed.

item.title: Self-medication of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder symptoms with psychoactive substances in adults: a scoping review of how symptom-relief motives are framed and operationalised across substances.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) use tobacco, cannabis, alcohol, cocaine and non-prescribed stimulants far more than the general population. The self-medication hypothesis holds that people with ADHD, including those undiagnosed, use substances to relieve core symptoms rather than for recreation or shared vulnerability to addiction, and is widely invoked to reframe illicit substance use as undiagnosed ADHD. How this claim is framed and tested has not been mapped across substances.

item.title: Disease management experiences of parents of children with ADHD: a qualitative directed content analysis.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The long-term management of children with ADHD primarily relies on parents. As primary caregivers, parents bear the main responsibility for their children's treatment coordination, daily behavior guidance, and school collaboration. However, the subjective experiences of these parents in navigating ADHD management, including their challenges, coping strategies, and emotional responses, remain insufficiently explored. METHODS: Face-to-face, semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted with 17 parents of children with ADHD.

item.title: The Influence of Policy on Early Diagnosis and Other Autism Services: A Narrative Review.
item.description: Little is known about how policy-laws, regulations, procedures, administrative actions, incentives, or voluntary practices of governments or other institutions-shapes access to early autism services including diagnosis before age three. Early diagnosis and treatment are considered critical to improve outcomes and to understanding how policy influences on such services could have substantial impact on outcomes for autistic children. We conducted a narrative literature review to determine what is known on how policy impacts early autism diagnosis and treatment.

item.title: The relationship between caregiver burden, depression, suicidal thoughts, and quality of life in patients' caregivers in the adult palliative service.
item.description: AIM: This study aimed to examine the relationships between caregiver burden, depression, suicidal ideation, and quality of life among caregivers of patients hospitalized in an adult palliative care unit and to identify factors associated with depressive symptoms. METHODS: This descriptive cross-sectional study included 75 caregivers of patients hospitalized in the Adult Palliative Care Unit of Erzurum City Hospital. Data were collected using the Caregiver Strain Index, Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D), Beck Scale for Suicide Ideation, (OPQOL)-Brief, and SF-36 Health Survey.

item.title: Teacher-student perceptual mismatch in positive co-experiences is associated with adolescent depression, bullying victimization, and suicidality.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Positive teacher-student interactions may be associated with adolescent mental health, but teachers and students may not experience the same interactions similarly. Integrating self-determination theory with the Operations Triad Model, we examined whether mismatch in positive teacher-student co-experiences was associated with adolescent mental health and whether mismatch direction mattered. METHODS: Cross-sectional paired data were analyzed from 1,836 students aged 11-17 years nested within 40 homeroom teachers in Hunan Province, China.

item.title: Epigenetics of generalized internet use disorder including data on overuse of social media: a closer look at the SLC6A4, NR3C1 and OXT genes.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Only few studies so far have investigated the molecular underpinnings of Internet Use Disorders (IUD), which can shed light on the neurochemical basis of excessive online behaviors. There are even less epigenetic studies in this research field, and longitudinal evidence is even more scarce.

item.title: Dynamic 18F-FDG PET characterizes age-related changes in fitted ventricular FDG kinetics in humans.
item.description: Ventricular cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) transport is an important component of intracranial solute movement and may contribute to glymphatic-associated transport pathways. However, clinically accessible methods for quantifying ventricular CSF tracer dynamics in humans remain limited. This study examined the potential of dynamic 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) for quantifying ventricular CSF tracer kinetics as an indirect measure of CSF transport by evaluating its association with age and clinical factors.

item.title: Epigenetic processes in depressive and anxiety disorders.
item.description: Depressive and anxiety disorders are the most common mental health problems, affecting millions of people worldwide, often leading to negative outcomes in all aspects of life, including work, family, and participation in community activities. These mental health problems exhibit considerable sex- and gender-based variations, with both depressive and anxiety disorders affecting women approximately twice as often as men.

item.title: Epigenetic mechnisms involved in posttraumatic stress disorder.
item.description: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a complex mental health condition influenced by various factors, including the environment, biology, and genetic variations. This chapter delves into how these factors interact, focusing on trauma exposure, brain mechanisms, and genetic expression changes that contribute to the development of PTSD.

item.title: Two clusters of brain regions with distinct age-related profiles of functional connectivity in autism spectrum disorder.
item.description: Brain functional connectivity changes throughout development, and individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may follow trajectories that differ from those of typically developing controls. Using large multisite resting-state fMRI cross-sectional datasets, we examined how functional connectivity differences between ASD and typically developing controls change across a broad age range of 5 to 64 y. A data-driven analysis identified two spatially distributed clusters of cortical regions showing distinct age-related profiles of ASD-TD connectivity differences.

item.title: Rightward Saccades Distort the Scaffold of Spatial Working Memory in ADHD.
item.description: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is typically characterized by executive dysfunction, yet emerging evidence points to spatially asymmetrical features of cognition. We examined whether transsaccadic working memory (tWM), the mechanism that integrates visual and motor signals across eye movements, shows directional vulnerability in ADHD. Participants with ADHD completed a spatial tWM task in which memory arrays (one or three items) were presented before leftward, rightward, or fixation trials, and repositioned a probe to the remembered target location.

item.title: A microexon regulatory code reveals autism-linked genetic variation.
item.description: Neuronal microexons are a highly conserved class of alternative splicing events enriched in genes with critical functions in nervous system biology1,2. Microexon splicing is often disrupted in the brains of autistic individuals, and mice with microexon deficiencies display autism-like phenotypes1,3,4. However, the full landscape of microexons is not known, and the impact of genetic variation on these exons has not been systematically investigated.

item.title: Association Between Vitamins Related to Brain Development and Sleep in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
item.description: PURPOSE: Sleep problems and nutritional abnormalities are common in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), yet the relationships between specific vitamin status, sleep characteristics, and ASD symptoms remain unclear. This study investigated the associations between neurodevelopment-related vitamin levels, sleep problems, and clinical features in children with ASD. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 605 children with ASD aged 2-7 years. Blood vitamin levels were measured using high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry.

item.title: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder polygenic risk score and incidence of cognitive impairment in older adults: A prospective multicohort study.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Preliminary evidence suggests a link between attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and later-life cognitive impairment. Whether genetic risk for ADHD, estimated using an ADHD polygenic risk score (ADHD-PRS), is associated with incident cognitive impairment (mild cognitive impairment or Alzheimer's disease dementia) remains unknown. METHODS: We analyzed 7761 cognitively unimpaired (CU) older adults with whole-genome sequencing from eight cohorts participating in the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project (ADSP).

item.title: Syndromic Autism in Helsmoortel-Van der Aa Syndrome: From Clinical Suspicion to Genetic Diagnosis.
item.description: Syndromic autism refers to autism spectrum disorder (ASD) occurring as part of an identifiable genetic syndrome. Helsmoortel-Van der Aa syndrome (HVDAS/ADNP syndrome) is a rare autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in the ADNP gene. We report a 10-year-old boy with ASD and intellectual disability who exhibited delayed motor and language development, characteristic facial dysmorphism, early tooth eruption, endocrine abnormalities, electroencephalography (EEG) abnormalities, and urogenital findings.

item.title: Changes in parent-rated attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder symptom scores and sleep parameters during individualized multidisciplinary clinical management in children with comorbid obstructive sleep apnea: a prospective cohort study in Vietnam.
item.description: OBJECTIVE: To describe changes in parent-rated attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptom scores, respiratory-polygraphy-derived parameters, and sleep characteristics over 6 months in children with ADHD and comorbid obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) who received individualized multidisciplinary clinical management. METHODS: This single-arm prospective cohort study was conducted at Vietnam National Children's Hospital from November 2022 to October 2024.

item.title: Opioids and the oxytocin system: Mechanistic interactions altering maternal neuroplasticity.
item.description: Due to the ongoing opioid epidemic, there has been a rise in the use of medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) during pregnancy. This paper examines how buprenorphine (BUP), the new golden standard for MOUD, may disrupt maternal care through dysregulation of the oxytocin (OXT) system. OXT is central to parturition, lactation, caregiving, and coordinating activity across the maternal brain network (MBN), including the paraventricular (PVN) and supraoptic nucleus, medial preoptic area, and nucleus accumbens.

item.title: Research and Outcome Priorities for the Canada Prenatal Nutrition Program in Ontario: A Community-Engaged Modified Delphi Study.
item.description: The Canada Prenatal Nutrition Program (CPNP) is a federal initiative that addresses the critical impact of early nutrition and perinatal care on health outcomes by providing community-based perinatal health and nutrition services to socially and economically vulnerable women and their infants. Using a flexible, locally adaptable community programming model, the CPNP aims to improve the health of women and their babies by promoting healthy birth weights and supporting breastfeeding; fostering community partnerships; and providing culturally sensitive support.

item.title: The Effect of Stimulant Medications on Symptom and Treatment Outcomes in Adults With Comorbid Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity and Substance Use Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The clinical question is whether stimulant medications are effective and safe for adults with co-occurring ADHD and substance use disorder (SUD), compared to non-stimulant or non-pharmacological treatments. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and nonrandomised comparative studies (NRCS) to inform treatment guidelines for this high-risk population.
FINDINGS: Six RCTs and one NRCS (total N = 662) were included. No significant differences were found between stimulant and non-stimulant/non-pharmacological treatments for ADHD treatment adherence, substance use outcomes, SUD symptom change, or substance abstinence (low confidence). A pooled analysis of three studies showed no significant difference in Clinical Global Improvement (OR 1.27, 95% CI 0.32–5.09). Evidence was insufficient to draw conclusions on ADHD symptom change, SUD treatment adherence, medication misuse/diversion, depression, or anxiety. No difference in adverse events was observed, but strength of evidence was not assessed.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is small, heterogeneous, and of low to very low quality, limiting firm conclusions. The absence of clear harm signals from stimulants is reassuring but preliminary. The lack of robust data on efficacy and safety, particularly regarding misuse/diversion and long-term outcomes, means current practice should remain cautious and individualised. More high-quality RCTs with longer follow-up are urgently needed.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: For now, stimulants can be cautiously considered for adults with co-occurring ADHD and SUD, especially long-acting formulations, but clinicians should monitor closely for misuse and diversion. Non-stimulants cannot be recommended based on current evidence. Shared decision-making and close follow-up are essential.

item.title: A comprehensive review of European clinical practice guidelines on psychological and cognitive assessment and support for cancer patients and their families.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review examined European clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) over the past 15 years to assess how they address psychological and cognitive assessment and support for cancer patients and their families, highlighting gaps in inclusivity and implementation.
FINDINGS: Thirty-eight CPGs were included, showing an increasing multidisciplinary focus primarily on adult cancer patients, with distress, anxiety, and depression as key targets. Common tools included the Distress Thermometer and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, while psychosocial support and counselling were the most recommended interventions. Digital and family-centred approaches were rarely mentioned, and heterogeneity was noted in evidence levels and recommendation strength.
INTERPRETATION: The review highlights a growing but inconsistent effort to integrate psycho-oncology into cancer care across Europe. Strengths include the breadth of included guidelines and focus on common symptoms, but weaknesses include limited inclusivity (e.g., underserved groups), scarce digital/family-centred interventions, and methodological heterogeneity. The evidence base for recommendations appears preliminary, with gaps in high-quality, standardised protocols.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Clinicians should be aware that while psycho-oncological support is increasingly recommended, access may vary by region and guideline quality. Digital and family-centred interventions remain underutilised and warrant further development and evaluation.
